title: Programmable growth of load-bearing solids

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a material system that uses living cells or cell-directed processes to accumulate material into a prescribed three-dimensional structural member. Programming would govern where material forms, how the member acquires its geometry, and when growth ends. The finished member would carry a specified engineering load under defined service conditions.

Engineered cells already provide a technical foundation for this direction through production, secretion and extracellular assembly of material constituents. The proposed advance combines that manufacturing capability with growth-directed geometry, controlled termination and verified structural performance. Continued metabolism in the finished member would depend on the implementation and any intended ongoing functions.

significance.text: Conditional synthesis. Achieving this capability would extend biological manufacturing to structural parts whose material and prescribed geometry develop together through controlled accretion. A direct consequence would be the ability to manufacture load-bearing members by programming their growth, including an endpoint at which they retain the required form and mechanical performance. The documented ability of engineered bacteria to assemble extracellular material constituents supplies a technical basis for this proposed extension.

Production directly from air, water and minerals would add a separate feedstock achievement. The reviewed study used laboratory culture media and identified feedstocks connected to carbon dioxide fixation as further work. Consequently, inexpensive environmental inputs and a closed materials-production loop remain conditional downstream possibilities. Their realization would require demonstrated feedstock conversion, with the necessary energy and other inputs accounted for.

Conditional synthesis. Building-scale use would require reliable geometry control across larger dimensions, joining methods, durability and qualification for the intended structural application. Growth as a manufacturing mechanism alone would establish neither code compliance nor lower cost or environmental impact. Those outcomes would require separate evidence about production resources, service life and practical deployment.

The analogy to living systems provides a broader research motivation. DOE's historical grand-challenge account discusses responsive materials, self-repair and metabolic or self-replicating pathways. Programmable structural growth would address one part of that vision. Self-repair, continued adaptation and replication would each require additional demonstrated functions.

missing_breakthrough.text: The integrated target is controlled biological or life-like accretion that produces a prescribed three-dimensional geometry, terminates predictably and delivers mechanical performance appropriate to a stated structural application. The supplied 2024 study establishes a cast-film manufacturing route. The reviewed evidence leaves the integrated structural-growth target undemonstrated, while the broader field's progress through 1 November 2026 remains unverified.

Engineering synthesis. Candidate barriers include coordinating material production with transport of nutrients and other required inputs, maintaining spatial control as thickness increases, and preserving the intended geometry during maturation or drying. A system would also need to coordinate its stopping cue with the development of load-bearing properties. These are concrete integration challenges inferred from the proposed capability. The supplied evidence does not establish which challenge would dominate a successful implementation.

Engineering synthesis. The relationship between biological activity and the finished material's service conditions remains an implementation question. An actively growing region could require conditions different from those of a mature structural region. Whether metabolism must persist throughout a dry finished member depends on its intended functions. The earlier formulation made continuous dry-state metabolism a universal requirement without establishing its necessity.

Engineering synthesis. Mechanical targets must be application-specific. Timber, concrete and metals offer different combinations of stiffness, strength, deformation and durability, so a general comparison with their structural range leaves the goal underspecified. The breakthrough needs a defined member geometry, loading mode and performance benchmark that connect material measurements to a credible structural use.

current_state.text: Manjula-Basavanna, Duraj-Thatte and Joshi reported compostable MECHS films in Nature Communications, volume 15, article 9179, published on 12 November 2024. The fabrication route treated and cast engineered E. coli biomass, followed by drying. The reported yield was 0.5–1 gram of film material per liter of bacterial culture. The abstract identified potential use in compostable primary packaging.

The paper reported Young's modulus tunable across approximately 6–450 MPa. For the CL1 crosslinked variant, the main-text account gave Young's modulus of 51.6 ± 18.4 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 1.6 ± 0.4 MPa. These quantities describe different mechanical properties, and the broad modulus range covers material variants. Establishing structural-member performance would additionally require geometry-specific loading evidence under stated conditions.

The methods reported a prototype film with lateral dimensions of 5 cm by 50 cm, fabricated from 6 liters of culture. Thus, tens-of-centimeters length was already demonstrated for a film. The relevant remaining distinction is whether growth generates the prescribed three-dimensional member geometry and yields verified structural performance. Sustained metabolism in the finished films, growth-directed structural-member formation and controlled termination of that structural growth were unestablished in the text assessed by the supplied review.

The supplied review assessed the main article's full text and matching paper PDF. Figure images and linked source-data spreadsheets were unavailable for inspection. A supplementary PDF had extraction warnings, which limited the use of its captions for independently validating plotted values. The quantitative results retained here were reported in the article's prose. These access limitations leave some underlying visual and numerical evidence unchecked.

DOE's historical grand-challenge page documents aspirations for materials that respond to their environment and repair themselves through capabilities analogous to living systems. Its historical context supports the research motivation. Establishing the contemporary status of programmable structural growth would require a current assessment of the field.

Evidence-scope synthesis. The supplied freshness record is empty, leaving field-wide progress and openness as of 1 November 2026 unresolved. The dated 2024 findings remain assessable within their reported film-fabrication scope. This record relies on the supplied review and source index, with no additional document inspection or research.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration. Starting from defined environmental feedstocks, a living or cell-directed system would grow a pre-specified three-dimensional member at least tens of centimeters long. Measurements during fabrication would establish how growth produces both the material and the prescribed geometry. External supports, molds, processing steps and supplied constituents would be documented so that the contribution of growth to the final form can be evaluated. Biological survival within a preformed block would establish only one component of this demonstration.
completion_criteria.label: Grow prescribed three-dimensional member at least tens of centimeters long

completion_criteria.text: Proposed termination test. An external or genetic cue would stop accretion within a declared time and geometric tolerance. Monitoring would establish the member's subsequent dimensional stability over a stated interval and under specified environmental conditions. Any further curing or maturation needed to achieve the tested mechanical properties would be documented.
completion_criteria.label: Cue-stopped accretion meets declared tolerances and maintains subsequent dimensional stability

completion_criteria.text: Proposed structural test. The member would meet a stated timber-comparable bending or compression benchmark. The protocol would identify the reference timber, member dimensions and cross-section, moisture conditions, loading configuration, loading duration and allowable deformation. It would report stiffness, load capacity and observed failure behavior as appropriate to the application. These choices would make the comparison evaluable and prevent length or cross-sectional size alone from determining success.
completion_criteria.label: Member meets a stated timber-comparable bending or compression benchmark

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries. Repeated production runs and independent replication would report dimensional accuracy, mechanical variability, growth time, yield and failure frequency. A bounded set of programmed geometries would establish the demonstrated breadth of shape control. Feedstock requirements, operating conditions, post-processing and the finished member's service limits would be stated explicitly. These are proposed completion criteria. Finite demonstrations would establish capability within the tested range.
completion_criteria.label: Repeated runs and independent replication quantify reproducibility and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis. MAS-02, Bulk structural solids that are both near their ideal strength and damage-tolerant, shares the concern with credible structural performance. MAS-07 centers on how a prescribed member is manufactured through growth. Near-ideal strength and exceptional damage tolerance would be additional material achievements, with their own verification requirements.

Roster-based synthesis. MAS-03, General atomically precise covalent construction, overlaps through programmable material assembly. MAS-07 could be realized through biologically organized accretion at coarser scales, with success measured by controlled member geometry and structural behavior. General atomic-level construction would require a different breadth and precision of assembly capability.

Roster-based synthesis. MAS-04, A reliable map from a property specification to a makeable material, could contribute methods for selecting compositions and growth programs that meet a structural target. MAS-07 requires an operating growth process and a demonstrated member. MAS-04 addresses a broader specification-to-material capability across materials and manufacturing routes.

Roster-based synthesis. MAS-09, Structural metals that fully recover from macroscopic fracture in service, overlaps with the broader aspiration for biologically inspired repair. Programmable growth concerns formation of a load-bearing member, while fracture recovery concerns restoration of a damaged member during service. Combining the two would require separate demonstrations of initial growth and post-fracture recovery.

Roster-based synthesis. MAS-05, Structural solids that remain engineering materials after fusion-level atomic displacement, shares the need to qualify mechanical performance under defined service conditions. Its defining challenge is radiation-damage tolerance. MAS-07's defining challenge is growth-directed manufacture, and any radiation-service capability would require additional evidence.

Roster-based synthesis. MAS-08, An ambient catalytic solid that fixes nitrogen at industrial intensity, has a possible enabling relationship if fixed nitrogen becomes a required growth feedstock. That connection depends on the chosen biological process and feedstock supply. MAS-08's industrial catalytic performance and MAS-07's programmed structural growth remain separate targets.

Roster-based synthesis. MAS-06, Reversible solids that store energy at chemical-fuel specific energy, MAS-01, Ambient-pressure room-temperature superconductivity in a manufacturable solid, and MAS-10, Topologically protected quantum matter outside the dilution refrigerator, concern functional properties that could eventually be incorporated into grown materials. The supplied evidence establishes no specific coupling to these capabilities. Each would retain its own energy-storage or quantum-material completion criteria alongside any growth-manufacturing demonstration.

change_log.reason: These capabilities retain the concept's identity and make its proposed advance explicit.

change_log.reason: The original opening overgeneralized how structural materials are produced.

change_log.reason: The supplied evidence establishes neither dry-state metabolism as a universal requirement nor a single decisive barrier.

change_log.reason: Biological production and engineered-living-material terminology alone do not establish continued viability or structural growth.

change_log.reason: Length alone cannot distinguish the proposed breakthrough from the existing film demonstration.

change_log.reason: The reviewed experiment used laboratory culture media and identified further feedstock development as future work.

change_log.reason: These details make success assessable while preserving the thresholds as proposals.

unresolved_issues: Field-wide progress through 1 November 2026 remains unverified because the supplied freshness record is empty.
The proposed structural benchmark still requires a reference timber, member dimensions, loading protocol, moisture conditions, loading duration and deformation limits.
The necessary role and duration of biological activity during growth, maturation and service depend on an implementation that has yet to be specified.
The dominant barriers among transport, spatial control, termination, maturation and mechanical performance remain unresolved.
Direct production from air, water and minerals requires separate feedstock-conversion evidence.
Figure images and linked source-data spreadsheets were unavailable to the supplied review, and supplementary extraction warnings limited independent validation of plotted results.
The supplied evidence does not establish sustained metabolism in the finished MECHS films or the integrated growth of a programmed load-bearing member.

brief.title: Growing solid parts that can carry weight
possible: Manufacturers could grow a structural part into a chosen shape using living cells or processes directed by them. Programming would control where material forms and when growth stops, leaving a finished part able to carry a specified load.
why: Biological manufacturing could produce structural parts whose material and shape develop together. For people making those parts, growth itself would become a way to achieve both the required form and the ability to carry weight.

sources.who: U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science
sources.showed: The department described research goals for materials that respond to their surroundings and repair themselves, drawing inspiration from living systems.
sources.cited_for: It explains the broader research motivation for giving materials capabilities found in living systems.
sources.not_established: These research goals do not demonstrate controlled growth of a structural part.

sources.who: Avinash Manjula-Basavanna, Anna M. Duraj-Thatte and Neel S. Joshi
sources.showed: They made compostable films, called MECHS, from engineered bacteria. They adjusted the films’ stiffness and stretchability by changing their composition and the proteins the bacteria produced.
sources.quote: MECHS films exhibit plastic-like stretchability, mechanical tunability, and skin-like healability.
sources.cited_for: Engineered bacteria can produce constituents for materials with adjustable mechanical properties.
sources.not_established: The films were cast and dried; they did not grow into programmed structural shapes with controlled stopping and demonstrated load capacity.

shown: Manjula-Basavanna and colleagues made bacterial films up to 50 centimeters long. They treated the bacterial material, cast it in molds and dried it. This demonstrates material production and adjustable properties, while the mold supplied the shape.
missing: A system must grow material into a prescribed solid shape, with growth itself determining the geometry.
A stopping signal must end material accumulation predictably and leave the part dimensionally stable.
A grown part must carry a defined structural load under stated conditions.
Repeated production and independent replication must establish consistency and practical limits.

milestones.label: Growth produces a prescribed structural shape
milestones.explanation: A system would have to grow a prescribed three-dimensional part tens of centimeters long from defined environmental inputs. Tracking growth and outside shaping aids would establish how growth creates its form.

milestones.label: A stopping signal leaves a stable shape
milestones.explanation: A signal would have to stop material accumulation within declared time and shape limits, followed by dimensional stability under stated conditions. This would establish control over the growth endpoint.

milestones.label: A grown part meets a timber performance benchmark
milestones.explanation: The part would have to meet a stated timber benchmark in bending or compression, meaning resistance to squeezing, under defined test conditions. This would connect material properties to a credible structural use.

milestones.label: Repeated and independent tests establish reliability and limits
milestones.explanation: Repeated runs and independent replication would have to measure consistency, production demands and service limits across a defined range of shapes. This would establish where the capability works reliably.

uncertain: The timber comparison still needs a reference material, test conditions and acceptable deformation limits.
How long cells must remain biologically active during growth, maturation and use depends on the design.
Direct production from air, water and minerals remains a separate challenge requiring demonstrated conversion and accounting for energy and other inputs.

page.title: Programmable living structural materials
page.definition: An engineered cellular system grows a structural member into a genetically specified three-dimensional shape and stops further material accumulation. The finished member meets the load and deformation limits of a stated structural application.

goal.need: UNEP estimates that constructing and operating buildings accounted for 34% of global CO₂ emissions in 2023, including about 2.9 Gt CO₂ of embodied emissions from construction. DARPA targets on-site growth of structural materials to replace shipment of finished materials with precursors and local resources.

figures.caption: Building-sector emissions in 2023
rows: Construction and operation: share of global CO₂ emissions
figures.note: These describe the existing sector; they are not estimates of savings from living materials.

statements.quote: engineer structural properties directly into the genomes of biological systems so that neither scaffolds nor external development cues are needed
statements.context: The long-term objective of the Engineered Living Materials programme, announced on 5 August 2016.

statements.quote: controlled production of made-on-demand living materials with multiple predictable dynamic functionalities, shapes and scales
statements.context: An objective of the EIC Pathfinder Engineered Living Materials challenge, published on 15 June 2021.

completion.title: A genetically grown structural member meets application-specific building-code requirements.
completion.criterion: A genetically programmed growth process produces a structural member with a preselected three-dimensional geometry. Material accumulation stops, and its shape and relevant mechanical properties remain within application-specific target ranges for one month. A member produced by that process passes tests establishing equivalency for a stated load-bearing use under 2024 IBC §§104.2.3.4–104.2.3.5. Growth generates the geometry; moulding or cutting alone does not satisfy this condition.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of DARPA growth and stability targets, EBRC termination objectives and International Code Council qualification provisions.
completion.basis: DARPA ELM, EIC Pathfinder, the EBRC materials roadmap, ISO/ASTM searches and IBC alternative-material provisions yielded separate biological and structural tests, but no integrated completion test. This synthesis joins programmed growth and termination to application-specific code equivalency; it adds no universal strength or size threshold.

milestones.title: Engineered cells secrete material-forming monomers or polymers without being destroyed.
milestones.criterion: Cells export material-forming monomers or polymers without cell destruction. Evidence: on 12 November 2024, Manjula-Basavanna et al. reported extracellular curli protein fibres from engineered E. coli and cast films yielding 0.5–1 g per litre of culture. A reported 5 cm × 50 cm prototype used 6 litres. Casting and drying supplied the film geometry; this result does not establish programmed structural growth.
milestones.set_by: Engineering Biology Research Consortium, Engineering Biology & Materials Science roadmap, Processing theme, page 29.
milestones.threshold_quote: Enable secretion of monomers or polymers without destruction of cells.

milestones.title: A cell lineage autonomously grows programmed three-dimensional shapes stable for at least one week.
milestones.criterion: A single engineered genotype develops from one progenitor cell into selectable three-dimensional shapes without experimenter-supplied developmental cues. Surface and interior cells remain distinguishable; size and shape remain stable for at least one week. Related evidence: Kim et al., published on 10 August 2022, used four cell-adhesion proteins and externally positioned bacterial seeds to grow two-dimensional patterns; the paper reports three replicates unless otherwise specified. This does not meet the autonomous three-dimensional test.
milestones.set_by: DARPA, DARPA-BAA-16-50, Track 2 Programmable-ELM, Task Area B: Programmable Shapes.
milestones.threshold_quote: The programmed size and shape must be stable in the developed system for at least one week.

milestones.title: Engineered material-producing cells arrest metabolism or undergo programmed death when their task ends.
milestones.criterion: Engineered cells arrest metabolism or undergo programmed cell death upon task completion, triggered externally or by sensing the relevant environmental condition. The roadmap gives no numerical stopping time. Related evidence: Heveran et al., published on 5 February 2020, used temperature and humidity switches to regenerate sand–gelatin materials through three generations, producing eight specimens from one parent. This demonstrates environmental control rather than an engineered task-completion response.
milestones.set_by: Engineering Biology Research Consortium, Engineering Biology & Materials Science roadmap, Properties & Performance theme, page 51.
milestones.threshold_quote: Engineer arrested metabolism or programmed cell death upon task completion

milestones.title: A grown material retains its shape and application-specific physical properties for one month.
milestones.criterion: Arbitrary shapes and relevant physical properties, including strength, density and porosity as applicable, remain stable for one month in the intended environment; target ranges must suit the application. Related evidence: Heveran et al. measured mechanics after seven days. Their 30-day viability assays found approximately 9% and 14% survival at 4 °C and 50% and 100% relative humidity, respectively, using five assay tubes per dilution. Cell survival does not establish one-month mechanical stability.
milestones.set_by: DARPA, DARPA-BAA-16-50, Track 1 Hybrid-ELM, Task Area A, Phase II milestone 4; this track permits mould-controlled geometry.

milestones.title: A biologically produced member passes code-equivalency tests for its intended structural use.
milestones.criterion: Tests establish equivalency to the 2024 IBC for the intended use in quality, strength, effectiveness, durability and applicable safety requirements. Test scale must predict end-use performance, and the testing party must be acceptable to the building official. Related evidence: MECHS CL1 films had tensile strength 1.6 ± 0.4 MPa and Young’s modulus 51.6 ± 18.4 MPa, with 15 biological replicates and values reported as mean ± standard deviation. These film measurements do not establish code equivalency.
milestones.set_by: International Code Council, 2024 IBC §§104.2.3.4–104.2.3.5, reproduced in ADM18-25 Part I of its 2025 IADMIN agenda; these provisions apply to alternative construction materials generally.
milestones.threshold_quote: be not less than the equivalent of that prescribed in this code

not_found: No published test combining programmed structural growth, controlled termination and load-bearing qualification was found in the programme, roadmap or standards searches.
No opened result demonstrated all three capabilities in one structural product.
The ICC-hosted 2024 IBC chapters could not be opened; the cited ICC committee agenda reproduces the relevant 2024 clauses.

results.finding: Engineered E. coli cultures produced 530 ± 188 mg of curli nanofibers per 500 mL; n = 6 biological replicates.
results.detail: The curli operon enabled protein secretion and extracellular assembly. Subsequent film fabrication used SDS treatment, casting and drying.
results.quote:
We estimated that 500 ml cultures of CsgA, CL1, and CL2 produced 530 ± 188 mg, 431 ± 159 mg, and 399 ± 154 mg of curli nanofibers, respectively (Fig.
3h
and Supplementary Fig.
9b
).

results.finding: MECHS CL1 films had a Young’s modulus of 51.6 ± 18.4 MPa; n = 15 biological replicates.
results.detail: The tensile measurements characterize film mechanics but do not establish 2024 IBC equivalency for a stated structural use.
results.quote:
The tensile tests of CL1 showed that their Young’s modulus (51.6 ± 18.4 MPa) and ultimate tensile strengths (1.6 ± 0.4 MPa) were twice that of CsgA only (i.e., not crosslinked) based MECHS films, (Fig.
3c, d, f
and Supplementary Figs.
7a
,
8a
).

results.finding: Single-genotype spheroids, seeded with 100 cells per well, formed two layers stable for 100 hours; replicate count not stated.
results.detail: The cells self-organized into distinguishable inner and outer layers, but the cultures began with 100 cells per well rather than one progenitor. Stability was reported for less than one week, and selectable shapes from one genotype were not demonstrated.
results.quote: These two-layer structures were stable for 100 hours.

results.finding: Engineered E. coli in printed material (n = 3) showed a nearly 100-fold reduction in colony-forming units after induction.
results.detail: The induced cells were embedded in the material; the experiment did not demonstrate metabolic arrest or programmed death upon completion of a material-production task. Cell growth subsequently recovered to some extent.
results.quote:
PQN4-MazF cells in the
printed structure were found to proliferate in the absence of
IPTG, but after 2 h of IPTG induction, the colony-forming unit
(CFU) count reduced by nearly two orders of magnitude due to
the expression of MazF (Fig. 4c).

results.finding: Printed biotic hydrogels (n=3 at day 2; n=5 at day 30) reached a storage modulus of 10.1 ± 1 kPa at day 30.
results.detail: The modulus increased from 5.4 ± 2 kPa at day 2, so mechanical stability was not demonstrated. The structures were printed, and the paper does not establish application-specific structural performance or stable arbitrary shapes.
results.quote:
Over the course of 30 days, the modulus
increased signiﬁcantly to 10.1 ± 1 kPa (P = 0.01) in the biotic case while
it did not change for abiotic samples (6.5 ± 1 kPa) (Fig.3e).

results.finding: Concrete containing ProZERO algae and biomineral blend reached 4,597 psi at 28 days; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The ready-mix example reports strength and claims ASTM C1157 compliance, but does not establish 2024 IBC equivalency across the required properties, end-use scale, or testing-party acceptability.
